html:
In 429 the Vandals and Alans, led by their king Gaiseric, crossed the Strait of Gibraltar from Spain into Roman North Africa, the richest grain land of the Western Roman Empire. Ancient sources say about 80,000 people made the crossing.

They marched east along the coast and besieged Hippo, where the bishop Augustine died during the siege in 430. In 439 Gaiseric took Carthage and made it his capital. With Carthage's fleet he raided the Mediterranean and in 455 sacked Rome.

The loss of Africa's taxes and grain was a heavy blow to the Western Empire. The Vandals were Arian Christians and often persecuted the Catholic clergy. Their kingdom lasted about a century, until Belisarius destroyed it in the Vandalic War of 533 to 534.
